Rocket Lab is an end-to-end space company delivering responsive launch services, complete spacecraft design and manufacturing, payloads, satellite components, and more – all with the goal of opening access to space. The rockets and satellites we build and launch enable some of the most ambitious and vital space missions globally, supporting scientific exploration, Earth observation and missions to combat climate change, national security, and exciting new technology demonstrations.
Our Electron rocket has become the second most frequently launched U.S. rocket annually and has delivered more than 230 satellites to orbit, all while we work to develop Neutron, our upcoming medium-lift, reusable launch vehicle for larger constellation deployment.

Our Space Systems business designs and builds our extensive line of satellites, payloads, and their components, including spacecraft that have been selected to support NASA missions to the Moon and Mars and components used on the James Webb Space Telescope.

Rocket Lab’s Space Systems Finance team is the business partner to the global Space Systems segment. We provide everything from financial results to strategic analysis, and everything in between, in order to drive results and intelligent business decisions that are best for Rocket Lab, our customers, and our stakeholders. We are flexible problem-solvers working in a fast-paced environment and thrive under the challenge of supporting this dynamic, high-tech space company.

Based onsite at Rocket Lab's Headquarters in Long Beach, CA the Finance Manager is responsible for supporting the finance cadences and analysis for the space systems segment. You will work with the satellite manufacturing and satellite components teams supporting the financial reporting, business cases, cost models and other adhoc analysis. In addition, you will drive many exciting projects to grow and advance the company.

Become a strong strategic partner to the Space System’s segment, providing timely and accurate financial information and recommendations to decision makers to make prudent business decisions
Support Rocket Lab space systems component businesses with the finance cadence; monthly financial reporting and analysis, quarterly forecasts, annual operating plan, etc.
Support, development, and maintenance of weekly and monthly financial reporting, planning, and KPI’s
Take point on dynamic business studies and adhoc analysis including detailed project ROI analysis.

8+ years of finance experience in a manufacturing company/environment and a bachelor’s degree or equivalent years of work experience (12+ years total experience)
In-depth experience with ERP, financial systems, and modeling
Expertise in the Microsoft Office Suite especially with Excel
Demonstrated experience implementing value add to the financial business process
Willingness to travel if necessary

The FP&A Senior Analyst is a key partner to Finance leadership and the wider business, driving data-driven decision making through planning, forecasting, and analysis. This role owns core FP&A processes, including budgeting, forecasting, management reporting, and variance analysis, and builds the financial models and insights that shape strategic and operational decisions across Showpad.

Develop and monitor key financial and business performance metrics (ie. ARR, bookings, EBITDA margin, and operating expenses).
Perform monthly and quarterly variance analysis (actuals vs. budget and forecast), explaining key drivers and trends to Finance leadership and business partners.
Build and maintain financial models for revenue, headcount, and operating expenses to support budgeting, scenario planning, and forecasting.
Manage the planning, forecasting and reporting processes across Showpad, both long-term and short-term, including but not limited to Quarterly Forecasts and the Annual Operating Plan.
Ensure the accuracy and completeness of company financial data, and contribute to identifying ways to remediate inconsistencies and streamline processes.
Identify actionable insights, suggest recommendations and influence the direction of the business by effectively communicating findings to cross-functional groups.
Build relationships with other departments and work together to establish best practices, proactively identify opportunities and streamline current processes & tools.

A Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field; a professional qualification (CFA, CPA, MBA) is a plus.
A mastery of Excel and g-sheets; must possess the ability to produce dynamic models and perform sensitivity analyses.
3-5 years of experience in Corporate FP&A or a closely related finance function, ideally with exposure to a SaaS or technology company.
Experience with reporting, budget process, and complex financial modeling.
Organized and detail-oriented; ability to work in situations with changing priorities and multiple simultaneous assignments.
Solid grounding in accounting principles.
Familiarity with SaaS business model and revenue drivers.

Ability to manage multiple priorities independently and meet tight deadlines. High level of integrity, professionalism, and attention to detail. Advanced proficiency in Excel; working knowledge of financial systems and reporting tools.

Our goal is to democratize publishing, commerce, and messaging so that anyone with a story can tell it, anyone with a product can sell it, and everyone can manage their communications from a single source.

About the Finance team
The Finance team ensures Affirm remains financially sound and strategically positioned for growth. Our team manages financial planning, accounting, pricing, vendor management, tax, investor relations, and corporate development. We deliver timely insights, accurate reporting, and careful analysis to support decision-making. From day-to-day financial operations to major investments, we enable sustainable, informed growth by maintaining strong fiscal discipline.

We are looking for a self-motivated and resourceful Bank Head of FP&A to join us during a pivotal moment of growth. As Affirm Bank is currently in its formation phase, we are actively building out our foundational team. Reporting to the Bank CFO, the Bank Head of FP&A will be central to this effort, playing a key role in the formation and operational build-out of the Bank.
The Bank Head of FP&A will play a critical role in building the team and leading day-to-day finance operations. Core responsibilities include managing the forecasting and budget process, developing robust financial models, capital stress testing and monitoring, financial analysis, and partnering with Affirm, Inc. cross-functional teams on financial workflows.

Team Leadership & Talent Development: Build and lead the Bank strategic finance team, providing strategic direction, recruitment, and coaching as we establish the function.

We are looking for a data-driven and operationally minded Senior Strategic Financial Analyst to serve as a key architect of our financial planning and reporting infrastructure. In this high-visibility role, you will go beyond traditional reporting to act as a strategic partner to our GTM, R&D, and Operations leaders.

You will not only track the numbers but also define how we track them—bridging the gap between our CRM (Salesforce) and Finance systems to ensure data integrity.

If you are a proactive problem-solver with 5+ years of experience who loves building models, optimizing deal structures, and uncovering insights that drive revenue efficiency, we want to hear from you. Key Responsibilities: 1. Strategic Planning & Metric Architecture
KPI Definition: Design and maintain a comprehensive set of SaaS metrics (e.g., ARR, NRR, CAC, LTV, Magic Number) to track performance across Revenue, R&D, and Support.
Financial Modeling: Build and refine sophisticated financial models to analyze revenue streams, customer segmentation, pricing strategies, and sales team productivity.
FP&A Leadership: Partner with the VP of Finance to drive the annual budgeting and quarterly forecasting process, incorporating real-time insights from operational data.
2. GTM Operations & Deal Desk Partnership
Deal Strategy: Serve as the financial partner to the Deal Desk and Sales Leadership; analyze pricing, deal profitability, non-standard contract terms, and revenue recognition implications, provide suggestions and input to define and shape the contract and order form structure
Compensation Analysis: Analyze the ROI of sales compensation plans and GTM organizational structure to ensure alignment with company growth targets.
Ad-Hoc Strategy: Conduct deep-dive analyses on specific business questions (e.g., new market entry, product margin analysis) to support executive decision-making.
3. Systems, Data Governance & Process Improvement
CRM to Finance Integration: Spearhead the integration between GTM systems (Salesforce) and financial systems (ERP/Planning tools).
Data Governance: Define the "source of truth" for sales data. Implement quality controls to ensure the accurate flow of booking and revenue data into financial reporting.
Process Engineering: Develop standardized operating procedures (SOPs) for financial analysis to move the department from ad-hoc reporting to scalable, automated frameworks.

Experience: 5+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, Strategic Finance, or Sales Operations and equivalent strong analytics experience for business strategies.
Industry Background: Prior experience in Enterprise SaaS company and prior private equity or investment banking experience preferred.

Advanced proficiency in Excel (complex modeling) is required.
Strong familiarity with Salesforce (reporting, dashboards, object relationships) is essential.
Experience with BI tools (e.g. Tableau, Power BI, Looker, Python) and Planning tools (e.g. Anaplan, Adaptive Insights) is a major plus.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Math, Accounting, Economics, or a related quantitative field. MBA or master degree is a plus.
Soft Skills: Proven ability to translate complex financial data into clear, actionable narratives for non-financial stakeholders (Sales, Engineering, Product). Strong communication skills and excellent writing skills. Strong team collaborator, self driven and motivated.

As a Budget Analyst (Recent Graduate), you will perform the following duties: Prepares initial budget estimates and justifications for assigned areas or programs in accordance with standard operating procedures.

Performs budget formulation, execution and administration work involving the monitoring of obligations incurred and the actual expenditures of funds. Compares obligations and expenditures to identify conditions of over or under obligation of funds.

Assists with reviewing and performing initial analysis of budget estimates and requests for allotments submitted by managers for accuracy of format, mathematical accuracy, adequacy of supporting narrative justification, and conformance with an organization's budgetary policy and guidelines.

Reviews organizational historical data and/or matches funding requests or projected costs to determine trends in spending and forecasts annual funding needs. Analyzes budget estimates and narratives for reasonableness and adequacy as it relates to increases, decreases, or change in the project scope or outcome.

EdOps ’s School Finance Manager position is ideal for school finance leaders ready to bring their expertise to a portfolio of schools and shape our nationwide finance offering alongside committed and experienced finance peers.
The School Finance Manager serves a portfolio of 5-8 schools, acting as those schools’ outsourced CFOs.

Like on-staff CFOs, they leverage team members to analyze backwards-looking financial data and deliver strategic financial advice aligned with their schools’ mission and goals, build relationships with school leaders and boards, proactively notice and solve client problems, and generally act as key members of clients’ leadership teams.

Our experience working with a wide range of schools – from newly authorized charter schools to independent schools with century-long histories, and from microschools to multi-campus networks – allows us to provide high-quality finance, accounting, and student data support across diverse educational environments.

Analyze, model, and solve problems on a wide range of business issues.
Engage in client listening and endeavor to proactively identify and solve clients’ financial challenges - either directly, or through engaging other teams at EdOps .

Solve small, real problems for schools on a daily basis.
Advise school leaders on nuanced, long term strategic financial decisions (i.e., facilities projects, staffing models, school expansion).
Develop close, trusting partnership with C-Level school leadership which will allow you to provide the best advice and support.
Present important financial information to a school’s Board of Directors.
Sharpen you expertise in strategic school finance, from multi-year budget development to internal process refinement
Work with 5-8 schools in different stages of growth and with different academic models.

Lead project-based or market development work beyond your school portfolio..
Continue to solve real problems, small and large, for schools every day.

ABOUT RENEW CAPITAL Renew Capital is a pan-Africa investment firm with a presence in 13 countries. We back the bold founders using technology to pursue Africa’s greatest opportunities. With more than a decade of investing on the continent, Renew Capital is among the most active investors building Africa’s thriving private sector.

Renew Capital is powered by a team of investment, finance, legal, advisory and market development professionals. Our bench includes seasoned investors, analysts, operators and ecosystem experts with deep experience scaling businesses across Africa.

ROLE SUMMARY The sr. financial analyst plays a critical role in evaluating, supporting and scaling high-potential ventures across Africa. This role sits at the core of Renew Capital ’s investment process, supporting sourcing, due diligence, investment decision-making and portfolio value creation.

The sr. financial analyst will work closely with investment managers, portfolio company CFOs and senior leadership, building rigorous financial models and translating complex data into clear insights that inform investment decisions. Responsibilities: The sr. financial analyst’s responsibilities are focused on three core areas: 1.

Investment Analysis & Due Diligence
Prepare and maintain robust financial models for pipeline and prospective investment opportunities.
Analyze historical financial data, forecasts and assumptions to assess risk, return, and scalability.
Evaluate capital expenditures, depreciation schedules, and capital structuring scenarios.
Conduct market sizing, competitive analysis and primary and secondary research to support investment theses.
Support financial and commercial due diligence processes from initial screening through investment committee review.
2. Portfolio Support & Monitoring
Work directly with portfolio company finance teams on budgeting, 13-week rolling cash flow forecasts, and financial controls.
Monitor portfolio company performance, identify trends, calculate key ratios, and flag risks or opportunities early.
Build and maintain strong working relationships with portfolio CFOs and founders.
3. Communication & Insight Generation
Translate complex analysis into clear, decision-ready materials for investment managers, leadership and the investment committee.
Prepare presentations, memos and dashboards that communicate insights concisely.
Collaborate with a diverse, distributed investment team across Africa using digital tools. QUALIFICATIONS
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business or a related field; MBA or Master’s in Finance preferred.
6–8+ years of progressive experience in financial analysis, investment analysis, private equity, venture capital, investment banking or corporate finance, with exposure to growth-stage companies.
Advanced financial modeling expertise, including integrated three-statement models, valuation, scenario and sensitivity analysis and capital structuring.
Strong experience supporting or leading financial and commercial due diligence processes.
Proven ability to translate complex financial analysis into clear, decision-ready insights for senior leadership and investment committees.
Excellent Excel and financial analysis skills, with experience working with large, complex data sets.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, and the ability to work effectively with investment teams, portfolio company CFOs and founders across diverse markets.
CFA or other recognized investment or financial modeling credentials preferred.
WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS As Renew Capital continues to expand its investment activity across Africa, strong financial analysis is essential to deploying capital responsibly and supporting portfolio companies through growth and complexity.

This role provides exposure to venture investing across multiple sectors and markets, with the opportunity to influence real investment outcomes. Wir bauen das AI-Driven Financial Operating System für das europäische Gesundheitswesen und lösen so die größten Herausforderungen für Patient:innen und Praxen. Damit schaffen wir, was keine Bank oder Softwareplattform bewältigen kann.

Daten in Handlungen übersetzen: Du baust Finanzmodelle und Dashboards, auf die sich Teams verlassen – nicht nice-to-have, sondern operativ entscheidend.

You'll own the relationship day-to-day, including the model itself and the reporting that keeps your business partner and FP&A leadership current — much of which you'll help build and improve as our systems mature — while working closely with your manager and the broader FP&A team when things get more complex.
You'll also be the primary finance point of contact for an executive-level functional leader — trusted enough to understand what they're trying to build and help them think through the trade-offs behind a hiring plan or a vendor contract. The best FP&A partners aren't gatekeepers; they're the person in the room who helps leaders find the path that gets them what they need within real constraints.
This role sits within Corporate FP&A and reports into the team's corporate and opex leadership. You'll partner closely with Accounting, People Ops, and the functional teams in your scope, and you'll routinely contribute to the materials that go in front of senior leadership — sometimes presenting them yourself. Automation is part of the job, not an aspiration: every recurring, manual piece of your workstream is something you're expected to notice and fix.
We work Flexible First . This role can be performed remotely anywhere in the U.S. or from our Oakland office.
The Impact You'll Have
Own opex forecasting and management for your function end-to-end. Build and maintain the monthly forecast for your area (e.g., Engineering opex, G&A opex), understand every driver of spend — headcount, vendor contracts, T&E, discretionary spend — and know the story behind variances before anyone has to ask.
Be the trusted finance partner to a functional leader. Sit in their planning meetings, understand their priorities, and help them structure decisions about headcount, vendor spend, and cost trade-offs. Bring solutions and options, not just numbers.
Own your workstream's reporting. Build and improve the model templates and reporting flows that keep your business partner and FP&A leadership current, help shape the dashboards and systems as our BI tooling matures, and flag every manual step worth automating.
Support the broader planning cycle. Own your portion of the annual operating plan and long-range plan, and run the monthly forecast cycle for your area, tying it back into the company-wide numbers Corporate FP&A owns.
Apply GAAP fluency within your scope. Model capitalized expenses correctly for your area, and help your business partners understand how their spend is treated — explaining amortization, capitalization, and cash versus accrual accounting in terms that make sense to them. Partner credibly with Accounting on the technical questions that come up in your workstream.
Contribute to senior leadership materials. Routinely build content that feeds board decks, exec reviews, and leadership updates — and present your own analysis directly in some forums.
Experiment with AI to make your workstream faster. Use AI tools to speed up modeling, reporting, and analysis, and bring ideas back to the broader team on what's actually working.

Background and experience. Bachelor's degree in a quantitative field (Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, Math, or similar); minimum 8 years of progressive FP&A experience, ideally including time at a scaled operating or public company.
A strong individual contributor who owns outcomes end-to-end. You've run a forecast, a process, or a cost center on your own — not just contributed pieces of it — and you're comfortable being the person accountable for the numbers.
Solid GAAP fluency. You understand capitalized expenses well enough to model them correctly, and you can explain amortization, capitalization, and cash versus accrual accounting to a non-finance business partner in simple terms. You know when a question is above your scope and needs an Accounting partner.
Comfortable with systems and allergic to manual work. You've built or maintained dashboards and model templates before, and your first reaction to a repetitive manual task is to look for a way to automate it.
A genuine business partner. You've worked directly with a functional leader before, you ask good questions, and you're trusted because you're useful — not because you're agreeable.
A clear communicator, comfortable presenting your own work. You can walk a VP or a room of senior leaders through your analysis without a translator, and you write and speak in plain, direct language.
Nice-To-Haves
Payments, fintech, or scaled SaaS experience
Public-company experience, including exposure to board or investor-facing materials
Hands-on experience with a BI/analytics platform (e.g., Sigma, Looker, Tableau)
Experience owning headcount or vendor-spend forecasting for a functional client group
Hands-on experience building AI-powered workflows, tools, or automations for finance work

Du möchtest dazu beitragen, aus vielen Gesellschaften eine integrierte, skalierbare und zukunftsfähige Finance-Plattform zu formen? Dann suchen wir genau Dich, zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt als:
(Senior) Finance Manager (m/w/d) - Corporate Finance & Transformation
Als (Senior) Finance Manager (m/w/d) - Corporate Finance & Transformation übernimmst Du eine zentrale Rolle beim Aufbau unserer gruppenweiten Finance-Funktion. Du sorgst dafür, dass neue Gesellschaften, Prozesse und Systeme erfolgreich in die Arsipa Gruppe integriert werden und schaffst die Grundlage für einheitliche, skalierbare und steuerbare Finance-Strukturen. Dafür brauchen wir Deine Unterstützung!
Die Arsipa Gruppe ist eine schnell wachsende, PE-backed Unternehmensgruppe im Bereich Health, Safety & Environment, unterstützt von Warburg Pincus.

Mit über 1.000 Mitarbeitenden, 20+ Tochtergesellschaften und 48 Standorten in Deutschland und Österreich bauen wir im Rahmen einer klaren Buy-&-Build-Strategie eine skalierbare Plattform mit nachhaltiger Wertschöpfung.

Unser Ziel: eine der führenden Anbieterinnen im deutschsprachigen Markt - unterstützt durch zentrale Funktionen wie Finance, HR, Marketing und IT am Standort Berlin.
Deine Aufgaben

Steuerung und Begleitung der Integration neuer Tochtergesellschaften in die Finance-Strukturen der Arsipa Gruppe.
Harmonisierung von Prozessen, Datenstrukturen und Reporting-Logiken über verschiedene Gesellschaften hinweg.
Unterstützung bei der Einführung gruppenweiter Standards im Accounting und Controlling.
Mitarbeit an Finance-Transformationsprojekten sowie der Weiterentwicklung unserer System- und Prozesslandschaft.

Analyse bestehender Finance-Prozesse und Identifikation von Optimierungspotenzialen.
Unterstützung bei der Einführung und Weiterentwicklung von Finance-, Reporting- und BI-Systemen.
Aufbau belastbarer KPI-, Reporting- und Steuerungsstrukturen.
Mitwirkung bei bereichsübergreifenden Projekten zur weiteren Professionalisierung unserer Finance-Funktion.

Enge Zusammenarbeit mit Group Accounting, Group Controlling / FP&A und unserem VP Finance sowie dem BI-Team.
Zusammenarbeit mit Geschäftsführungen unserer Tochtergesellschaften.
Steuerung und Abstimmung mit externen Beratern, Wirtschaftsprüfern und weiteren Stakeholdern.
Deine Startvoraussetzungen

Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Finance-Umfeld mit fundiertem Verständnis von Accounting- und/oder Controlling-Prozessen, idealerweise ergänzt durch Erfahrung in Finance Transformation, Consulting, CFO-Office, Corporate Finance oder FP&A Erfahrung in der Steuerung komplexer Projekte sowie im Umgang mit unterschiedlichen Stakeholdern.
Fließende Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse.

s.h: Das hilft Dir, schneller erfolgreich zu sein
s.t:
Ausgeprägtes analytisches Denkvermögen sowie Interesse an Prozessen, Daten und Systemen (idealerweise DATEV, LucaNet).
Strukturierte, pragmatische Arbeitsweise sowie idealerweise Erfahrung in PE-/VC-getriebenen Unternehmen oder dynamischen Wachstumsfeldern.

Attraktives Arbeitsumfeld: 30 Tage Jahresurlaub, Heiligabend und Silvester jeweils einen halben Tag frei, ein hybrides Setup mit einem Homeoffice-Tag pro Woche sowie ein zentral gelegenes Office im Rocket Tower inklusive Gym, unmittelbar an der U-Bahn-Station „Kochstraße“.
Starke Teamkultur: Eine offene und wertschätzende Unternehmenskultur mit regelmäßigen Stand-ups, monatlichen All-Hands Meetings und gemeinsamen Events zur Förderung einer positiven und kollegialen Arbeitsatmosphäre.
Direkte Nähe zur Finance-Führung und zum Business: Du arbeitest eng mit unserem VP Finance, dem CFO sowie den Geschäftsführern unserer Tochtergesellschaften zusammen und unterstützt aktiv den Aufbau unserer gruppenweiten Finance-Funktion.
Gestaltungsspielraum in einer Buy-&-Build-Plattform: Du gestaltest Prozesse, Strukturen und strategische Initiativen in einer krisensicheren, rasant wachsenden Unternehmensgruppe aktiv mit und erhältst Einblicke in die Umsetzung einer Roll-up-Strategie – unterstützt durch einen der weltweit führenden Investoren, Warburg Pincus.
Einblicke in die Finance-Transformation einer PE-backed Unternehmensgruppe: Von der Integration neuer Gesellschaften über die Standardisierung von Prozessen und Systemen bis hin zu Reporting-, Governance- und Skalierungsprojekten wirkst du an zentralen Finance-Initiativen unserer Buy-&-Build-Strategie mit.

Our US Partner is a reputable mid-sized New York law firm known for its collaborative culture and business-focused approach, providing full-service legal support across litigation, real estate, corporate law, labor and employment, and intellectual property.

We are looking for a highly analytical and detail-oriented Senior Financial Analyst to support financial planning, reporting, and data analysis for our client. The ideal candidate will have strong experience in budgeting and forecasting, advanced expertise in SQL and Excel, and prior experience working in a law firm environment.

This role requires someone who can translate complex financial data into actionable insights and support strategic decision-making. This is a full-time role, on a US shift, and a work-from-home set-up.

If you have strong technical and financial skills and enjoy working in a data-driven environment, this may be your opportunity to join a growing organization. DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Develop and maintain financial models to support budgeting, forecasting, and long-term planning.
Perform advanced SQL reporting and analysis related to accounts payable, revenue, and profitability.
Conduct detailed profitability analysis across clients, matters, practice groups, or service lines to identify margin trends and improvement opportunities.
Analyze accounts payable and revenue data to support internal budgeting and forecasting processes.
Create, modify, and maintain SQL queries and automated reports from the companys database.
Automate financial and operational reporting, including scheduled email reporting to stakeholders.
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports, including variance and margin analyses.
Partner with leadership and department heads to support forecasting, budgeting, and financial performance initiatives.
Identify trends, risks, and opportunities through data analysis and provide actionable recommendations.
Ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial data across systems and reports.
Support ad hoc financial analysis and executive-level reporting as needed.

Minimum of 5 years of experience in financial analysis, financial planning, or similar roles.
Preference for candidates with a legal firm background or experience in professional services.
Demonstrated experience performing profitability and margin analysis to support budgeting and strategic decision-making.
Strong expertise in SQL, including the ability to create and modify queries and reports.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including complex formulas, financial modeling, and data analysis.
Proven experience in budgeting, forecasting, accounts payable analysis, and revenue analysis.

s.h: Experience automating reports and workflows is highly preferred.

Model pipeline health, sales dynamics, funnel economics, and enterprise sales performance to help leadership understand the drivers behind growth.

Support pricing and packaging analysis, including the impact of commercial decisions on revenue and margin.

Define the KPIs, reporting cadence, and frameworks that improve decision-making, including a consistent approach to marketing ROI, CAC, conversion, and marketing-sourced bookings.
Present clear, concise recommendations to Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and executive leadership, including board-level audiences when required.

Partner with RevOps on capacity planning, funnel performance, and the financial implications of GTM strategy.
Work with Data and Controlling to turn GTM financial reporting into tangible insight and recommendations rather than simply explaining variances.

Use AI and automation to create repeatable, scalable planning and reporting workflows that reflect how an automation company should operate.

Must-haves
📊 FP&A expertise: You have 7+ years of experience in FP&A or strategic finance, ideally within a fast-paced technology or B2B SaaS environment.
🗂️ Complex planning leadership: You have led multi-entity, multi-stakeholder annual planning, budgeting, and forecasting processes from end to end.
🤝 GTM business partnering: You have partnered closely with Sales and Marketing leaders, ideally supporting a sales-led growth or enterprise sales motion.
📈 Enterprise sales economics: You are fluent in CAC, CAC payback, CLV-to-CAC, pipeline dynamics, funnel conversion, and the economics of enterprise growth.
🧮 Financial modeling: You build sophisticated, integrated financial models that remain reliable as assumptions and business conditions change.
🗣️ Executive communication: You turn complex financial analysis into clear recommendations and are comfortable presenting to GTM leaders, executives, and board audiences.
🤖 AI- and automation-first mindset: You actively use AI and automation platforms such as n8n to improve the quality, speed, and repeatability of your work.
Nice-to-haves
🎓 Relevant education: You have a degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, or a related field.
🏦 Transaction experience: You started your career in transaction advisory, investment banking, or a similarly analytical environment.
🐍 Python skills: You are comfortable using Python to automate modeling, analysis, or reporting workflows.
🧩 Planning platforms: You have worked with financial or headcount planning platforms such as Pigment in complex, multi-entity environments.

🗄️ SQL capability: You can use SQL or another query language to retrieve and shape data independently.
🌱 PLG familiarity: You understand product-led growth metrics and motions and can collaborate effectively with PLG and R&D finance counterparts.
📊 BI experience: You have worked with dashboarding or BI tools such as Looker, Tableau, or Power BI.
⚙️ Relevant industry exposure: You have experience in workflow automation, developer tools, infrastructure software, or a related SaaS category.
🌍 Distributed collaboration: You are comfortable working in a distributed, async-first team with a high degree of autonomy.

The VA has adopted Core Values and Characteristics that apply universally across the Department. The five Core Values define "who we are," our culture, and how we care for Veterans, their families and other beneficiaries. The Values are Integrity, Commitment, Advocacy, Respect and Excellence ("I CARE").

That's why we created the Technical Career Field (TCF) Program - one of the largest training programs at VA. TCF positions equip professionals (including veterans) with the specialized knowledge they need to support the delivery of quality health care for our Nation's veterans.

TCF is a national workforce development program within VHA designed to replenish technical staff in critically identified positions. The TCF career fields represent those technical areas where VA-specific knowledge and experience are essential for success.

Selectees will follow a structured two-year individual development plan and will receive training and mentorship from a subject matter expert (preceptor). Trainees must remain at the hiring grade for a minimum of one year. Selectees will also be required to sign Mobility, Training, and Continued Service Agreements.

The TCF career fields represent those technical fields where VA-specific knowledge and experience is desirable for success in the field. Individuals selected follow a formal training plan for two years during which they are trained, coached, and supervised by a preceptor.

As part of the VA's succession planning, the Technical Career Field (TCF) training program was created to ensure individuals are trained in critical areas that have current or predicted shortages. The program is nationally funded to include salary, benefits and training/travel dollars.

At the time of acceptance into the TCF program, trainees will be asked to sign mobility, training, and service agreements. Relocation expenses for acceptance into the training program or for placement are not funded by the TCF program.

Please keep in consideration, the training program is meant for those individuals who plan on staying with the VA a minimum of 3 years after completion of their training program. Selectees will be required to complete and sign the following paperwork; Mobility, Training, and Continued Service Agreements.

Although not guaranteed, with more than 150 freestanding facilities and hundreds of clinic locations, we will strive to place trainees in positions that will work for their needs and the needs of the VA.

As a Financial Analyst, you will: Perform independently financial analysis and evaluation duties in assignments of limited difficulty.

Independently applies established methods and procedures, clearly applicable statutory or regulatory provisions, and standard practices and techniques to perform a full range of duties involved in less difficult assignments. Prepare less difficult accounting and financial analyses and presentation materials.

Perform studies, research projects, and perform a wide range of technical duties. Develop alternatives and recommended financial policies within the context of BPA's strategic financial goals and objectives. Research and analyze financial issues related to development, communication, and execution of BPA's financial strategy and objectives.

Prepare briefings materials and analyses on issues, problems, and findings related to financial topics.
SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS GS-09: A qualified candidate's resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-07) in the Federal service.

GS-09 Specialized experience is defined as: 1) Perform financial analysis and evaluation duties in a developmental capacity; apply established methods, regulatory provisions, and standard practices to independently perform less difficult assignments; 2) Research and analyze financial issues to develop alternatives and recommended financial policies within the context of BPA's strategic financial goals and objectives.

You may substitute education for specialized experience as follows: Master's or equivalent graduate degree; or 2 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree; or a LL.B. or J.D. if related; your education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. -OR- Combination of education and experience as described above.

Less than one year of specialized experience may be combined with graduate education in excess of the amount required for the next lower grade level (i.e., credit hours beyond the first year of full-time study may be credited).

One academic year of graduate education is considered to be the number of credits hours the graduate school has determined to represent one academic year of full-time study. If the graduate school's definition of one year of graduate study is not available, 18 semester hours (or 27 quarter hours) is used.

When crediting education that requires specific course work the number of hours of related courses required, as a proportion of the total education, is prorated. GS-11: A qualified candidate's resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-09) in the Federal service.

GS-11 Specialized experience is defined as: 1) Perform financial analysis and evaluation duties in assignments of average difficulty; apply established work methods and pertinent regulatory provisions to resolve financial and management problems; 2) Research, formulate, and assess alternative and recommended financial policies within the context of BPA's strategic financial goals and objectives.

You may substitute education for specialized experience as follows: Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree; or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to such a degree; or a LL.M., if related; your education must demonstrate the knowledge, skills, and abilities necessary to do the work. -OR- Combination of education and experience as described above.

Less than one year of specialized experience may be combined with graduate education in excess of the amount required for the next lower grade level (i.e., credit hours beyond the first two years of full-time study may be credited).

One academic year of graduate education is considered to be the number of credits hours the graduate school has determined to represent one academic year of full-time study. If the graduate school's definition of one year of graduate study is not available, 18 semester hours (or 27 quarter hours) is used.

When crediting education that requires specific course work the number of hours of related courses required, as a proportion of the total education, is prorated. "Experience" refers to paid and unpaid experience.

Examples of qualifying unpaid experience may include: volunteer work done through National Service programs (such as Peace Corps and AmeriCorps); as well as work for other community-based philanthropic and social organizations.

Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills; and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

s.h: HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT -
s.t:
BestDrive, a subsidiary of Continental, is seeking a strategic and results-oriented Finance Manager to lead finance, accounting, pricing, procurement, and investment controlling functions supporting our retail and plant operations across North America.
This leadership role partners closely with executive leadership and Continental's Accounting and Controlling teams to drive financial performance, strengthen internal controls, improve operational efficiencies, and provide strategic business insights that support continued growth.
If you're a collaborative finance leader who enjoys influencing business decisions through data and financial strategy, we'd love to hear from you.

s.h: As the Finance Manager, you will
s.t:
· Lead the month-end close process and ensure accurate, timely financial reporting.
· Oversee budgeting, forecasting, financial planning, and variance analysis.
· Manage intercompany accounting, reconciliations, and financial controls.
· Develop financial reporting, KPIs, and Power BI dashboards to support business decisions.
· Lead Procure-to-Pay (P2P) operations and drive continuous process improvements.
· Partner with leadership on capital investment planning, business cases, and financial analysis.
· Develop pricing strategies that support growth while maximizing profitability.
· Lead procurement activities, supplier strategies, and purchasing governance.
· Support internal and external audits while maintaining compliance with GAAP, IFRS, and company policies.
· Coach, develop, and lead a high-performing finance team.

s.t:

· 7-10 years of progressive accounting, finance, or controlling experience
· 3-5 years of leadership experience
· Experience with:
o Financial Accounting
o Month-End Close
o Budgeting & Forecasting
o Financial Planning & Analysis (FP&A)
o Intercompany Accounting
· Intermediate Power BI experience
· Strong analytical, communication, and leadership skills

About Passionfroot
Creator-led growth is one of the fastest-growing channels in B2B - we're building the infrastructure behind it.
Passionfroot is the leading platform where modern companies scale creator-led growth, and where top creators manage and monetize brand partnerships.
Our customers are some of the most ambitious, fastest-moving companies in the world - Replit, Figma, Framer, LumaAI, Gamma, Airtable - companies that set the standard for what modern growth looks like. We help them run high-impact creator programs across LinkedIn, YouTube, newsletters, and more.
We're growing 13x in revenue YoY, profitable, and backed by some of the best VCs in the world including Creandum and a top-tier US VC (more on that very soon 👀) and founders and operators from Cursor, Anthropic, n8n and more. We're expanding fast across New York, Europe, and Brazil - and we're just getting started.

We're growing 13x YoY - and growing that fast only works if we know exactly which number we're growing toward, and why. That's what this role is for.
Working closely with the Head of Operations, you'll set ambitious financial targets for the whole company, then own the thinking that gets us there: knowing our P&L and balance sheet inside out, understanding exactly what it takes to hit the number, and turning that into a plan the whole team can rally around.

You'll be the person everyone trusts to say clearly where we stand, what's needed to close the gap, and what has to happen next - across accounting for both our US and German entities, revenue, and how the company spends and pays its people.

Own the numbers
Stay on top of our P&L and balance sheet, keeping them accurate and up to date. Own accounting for both our US and German entities in-house - running monthly reconciliations, closing the books, handling tax filings and compliance, and making sure our financials are clean and audit-ready in both jurisdictions.
Help set the company's financial targets
Partner with the Head of Operations to set financial targets for the whole company, and track performance against them.
Own revenue operations
Run revenue operations end to end - from invoicing and billing to reconciliation and reporting - so revenue data is always accurate and easy to trust.
Own expenses and payroll
Manage company expenses and own salary payouts, making sure everyone gets paid accurately and on time, and that spending is tracked and controlled.

3+ years of experience in finance, accounting, or a similar operations/finance role, ideally in a startup environment
Experience with, or comfortable quickly learning, accounting across multiple jurisdictions - ideally US and Germany
Understands the German accounting and tax system, and speaks German
Strong understanding of P&L and balance sheet fundamentals
Comfortable owning revenue operations and financial processes end to end
Highly organized, detail-oriented, and trustworthy with sensitive financial information
Obsessed with accuracy - you catch errors before they become problems
Moves fast and communicates proactively - your teammates always know where things stand
Excited to build and improve financial processes, not just execute one-off tasks
Success in this role looks like
P&L and balance sheet are accurate, up to date, and easy for leadership to act on
